roundtrip: serialize/deserialize or encode/decode preserves the declared behavior.
input-immutability: APIs do not mutate caller input unless documented.
invalid-input: Invalid input fails predictably and does not corrupt state.
package-boundary: Public imports do not accidentally pull forbidden dependencies or heavy modules.
request-shape: Generated requests match the declared protocol contract.
response-decoding: Supported responses decode to typed values; unsupported responses fail clearly.
retry-idempotence: Retries do not duplicate irreversible effects in the local model.
replay: An emitted event, patch, or operation log replays to the same state.
idempotence: Duplicate messages or operations are safe where the contract requires it.
convergence: Replicas reach the same final observable state after healing or replay.
out-of-order: Out-of-order delivery preserves final state or fails by contract.
resource-limit: Large or adversarial inputs respect explicit time, size, or count caps.
parse-print-parse: Printing and reparsing preserves the meaningful program structure.
optimization-equivalence: Optimized output is semantically equivalent to unoptimized output.
diagnostic-stability: Errors and warnings stay deterministic enough for tests and users.
